q: What is the allowable MAXIMUM total gross floor area applicable to the existing lot, in square meter?
n: For the given institutional corner lot without sprinklers, the BHL (5 storeys) × 60% gives 3.0 × 6,195 m² = 18,585 m² maximum TGFA. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1 (TGFA limitation); data in the item's brief.

q: What is the total gross floor area, inclusive of decks, platforms and balcony, of the existing building, in square meters?
n: Enclosed area 2,431 m² plus the decks, platform and balcony gives a TGFA of about 3,420 m² for the existing building. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (TGFA definition); data in the item's brief.

q: What is the, total gross floor area, inclusive of decks, platforms and balcony, of the expanded building, in square meters?
n: Adding the 1,375 m² hall: 3,420 + 1,375 = 4,795 m² TGFA for the expanded building. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII; data in the item's brief.

q: Given that the front deck is elevated by 150mm from front sidewalk & front yard, what is the MINIMUM length of the front ramp entrance in meters?
n: With a maximum ramp slope of 1:12, a 150 mm rise needs 150 × 12 = 1,800 mm, so 1.80 m of ramp. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), ramps.

q: Given that the front deck is elevated by 0.15 meter from the front sidewalk and front yard, what is the riser height of the entrance steps, the number of which is as per MINIMUM required?
n: A 0.15 m rise needs only one step, so its riser is 0.15 m, within the 150 mm accessible maximum. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), stairs; NBC IRR Sec. 1207.

q: The approximate total enclosed area of the existing building is ___ square meters.
n: Ground floor 1,903 m² + second-floor offices and stairwell 528 m² = 2,431 m² enclosed area. Source: Data in the item's brief.

q: The approximate total enclosed area of the expanded building is ___ square meters.
n: 2,431 m² existing + 1,375 m² hall = 3,806 m² enclosed area after expansion. Source: Data in the item's brief.

q: What is the MINIMUM floor-to-floor height of the building in meters, if 0.60-meter-high space is for beams and utilities?
n: A 2.70 m minimum ceiling (naturally ventilated first storey) + 0.60 m for beams and utilities = 3.30 m floor-to-floor. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 805; data in the item's brief.

q: How many approximate cubic meters of ready mix- concrete were used for the existing 2nd floor slab.of 100mm thick with steel. decking underlay?
n: The second-floor slabs (offices, stairwell, balcony) total about 690 m² × 0.10 m = 69 m³ of ready-mix concrete. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (volume method); data in the item's brief.

q: Which figure uses diagrid structural technology?
n: Figure C is wrapped in a diagonal grid of members, a diagrid structure. Source: CTBUH, Diagrid Structural Systems; Ching.

q: Which figure utilizes glass curtain wall technology?
n: Figure E is a glass box with a curtain-wall facade. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which figure uses a steel frame and sandwich panel system?
n: Figure A shows a steel frame clad with sandwich (insulated) panels. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which technology is most suitable for large building spaces?
n: Thin shells, as in Figure D, span large column-free spaces most efficiently, which suits large building spaces. Source: Schodek, Structures; Ching.

q: What is the elastic movement of loaded parts of a structure?
n: Deflection is the elastic movement (displacement) of loaded parts of a structure. Source: NSCP 2015, Chapter 2 (definitions); Gere & Goodno.

q: What is the effect of earthquake motion acting in directions other than the one being checked?
n: The orthogonal effect is the effect of earthquake motion acting in directions other than the one being checked. NSCP combines 100% in one direction with 30% in the other. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.8.1 (orthogonal effects).

q: What is the ratio of longitudinal stress to strain within the elastic limit?
n: The modulus of elasticity (Young's modulus) is the ratio of normal stress to strain within the elastic limit. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is the horizontal displacement of one level relative to the level above or below?
n: Story drift is the lateral displacement of one level relative to the level above or below. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (definitions).

q: What gap keeps adjacent structures from pounding during seismic or wind sway?
n: Building separation is the gap that keeps adjacent structures from pounding during seismic or wind sway. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.7.2.11.

q: Which system has a near-complete space frame for gravity loads, with shear walls or braced frames resisting lateral loads?
n: A building frame system has an essentially complete space frame for gravity loads, with shear walls or braced frames resisting lateral loads. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.4.6.

q: Which frame, fixed at its supports, resists deflection best but is sensitive to settlement and thermal movement?
n: A fixed frame, rigidly fixed at its supports, resists deflection best but is sensitive to settlement and temperature change. Source: Schodek, Structures.

q: What is a rigid frame of two columns and a beam forming one bay?
n: A portal frame is a rigid frame of two columns and a beam forming one bay. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which system lacks a complete vertical load-carrying space frame?
n: A bearing wall system lacks a complete vertical load-carrying space frame. Walls carry the gravity loads. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.4.6.

q: What is a three-dimensional system, without bearing walls, of interconnected members acting as one unit?
n: A space frame is a three-dimensional system of interconnected members, without bearing walls, acting as one unit. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (definitions).

q: The live load on a structure resulting from the weight of people, furniture, stored materials, and other similar items within a building.
n: Occupancy load (live load) is the load from people, furniture, stored materials and similar items. Source: NSCP 2015, Chapter 2, Sec. 205.

q: What is the total design lateral force at the base of a structure?
n: Base shear (V) is the total design lateral force at the base of a structure. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.5.2.

q: Which structures must stay operational after an earthquake?
n: Essential facilities, such as hospitals and fire stations, must stay operational after an earthquake. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 103-1 (occupancy categories).

q: What is it called when a structure's natural period matches the ground motion's dominant period?
n: When a structure's natural period matches the dominant period of the ground motion, resonance amplifies its response (soil–structure resonance). Source: Chopra, Dynamics of Structures; NSCP 2015 Sec. 208.

q: What is any condition, such as fracture, buckling or yielding, that makes a structure unfit for service?
n: Structural failure is any condition (fracture, buckling, yielding) that makes a structure unfit for service. Source: NSCP 2015 (definitions).

q: What is the upper, flexible part of a structure made of a vertical combination of systems?
n: In NSCP terminology a tower is the upper, more flexible part of a structure formed by a vertical combination of systems. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (definitions).

q: According to standard sign conventions for moments:
o: A positive moment is counterclockwise, and a negative moment is clockwise
A positive moment is clockwise, and a negative moment is counterclockwise
The direction of the moment does not matter
n: When summing moments, many statics texts and reviewers take clockwise moments as positive and counterclockwise as negative. Any consistent convention gives the same result. Source: Hibbeler, Engineering Mechanics: Statics (sign conventions).
